root_cause.text: The re-application of a global ASPM check (amdgpu_aspm = 0) after the per-device refactoring of the amdgpu_aspm parameter created a mismatch between global and per-device state, causing crashes on multi-GPU systems where only some GPUs support ASPM.
root_cause.evidence: The patch reverts commit 7294863a6f01248d72b61d38478978d638641bee, which added `if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)) amdgpu_aspm = 0;` in amdgpu_pci_probe. The CVE and commit message state this caused "very hard to debug crashes, when used with a system with two AMD GPUs of which only one supports ASPM" and that the commit was erroneously applied after commit 0ab5d711ec74 ("drm/amd: Refactor `amdgpu_aspm` to be evaluated per device") removed the old global logic.

The CVE and commit message state this caused "very hard to debug crashes, when used with a system with two AMD GPUs of which only one supports ASPM" and that the commit was erroneously applied after commit 0ab5d711ec74 ("drm/amd: Refactor `amdgpu_aspm` to be evaluated per device") removed the old global logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix automatic ASPM overriding behavior by removing the probe-time check that forced ASPM off when the device had ASPM disabled.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional block that set amdgpu_aspm to 0 when amdgpu_aspm was -1 (default) and PCIe ASPM was not enabled on the device at probe time.
intent_record.how: Previously, the driver would automatically disable ASPM functionality by setting amdgpu_aspm=0 if the device did not have ASPM enabled during probe and the module parameter was left at default. After removal, the driver will not override the amdgpu_aspm parameter based on the initial ASPM state, allowing the default value (-1) to persist and potentially enabling dynamic ASPM control.

grouping_result.intent: Fix automatic ASPM overriding behavior by removing the probe-time check that forced ASPM off when the device had ASPM disabled.

relevance_review.reason: Group 0 directly addresses the root cause by removing the probe-time check that forced ASPM off globally, which caused the mismatch between global and per-device state on multi-GPU systems.

candidates.rationale: This global assignment forces ASPM off for all devices based on a single device's ASPM status, causing crashes on multi-GPU systems where only some GPUs support ASPM.

vuln_statements.explanation: This global assignment forces ASPM off for all devices based on a single device's ASPM status, causing a mismatch with per-device state and crashes on multi-GPU systems where only some GPUs support ASPM.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds a global assignment `amdgpu_aspm = 0` when `pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)` is false. This modifies a global variable based on a per-device condition, which can cause a mismatch on multi-GPU systems where only some GPUs lack ASPM support. The code does not include any per-device handling to avoid affecting other GPUs, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
